message:
Bug: the post-deploy watch counts a person's usage limit as failed turns, so it blames an innocent deploy and wakes its minion for nothing. Use citadel:bug-fixing.

Evidence (2026-11-16): the watch mailed the Taskmaster "after Nov 16, 13:27 PST (deploy a03f130e), failed turns went from 2% (1 of 59) to 12% (8 of 68)" and woke #805. All 8 "failed" turns ended between 14:02 and 14:03 PST. Each turn's result event says `"is_error":true` with the result "You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3:30pm (America/Los_Angeles)". So one account ran out of usage; the deploy did nothing wrong. #805 spent a turn finding that out.

Cause: `turnOutcomes` in src/db.ts (~line 2745) counts every turn whose result event has `"is_error":true`, usage-limit and rate-limit stops included. deploy-watch.ts compares those counts before and after a deploy.

Fix: leave turns that stopped on a usage or rate limit (find how the runner already recognises them, e.g. where it parks a minion for "the usage limit") out of both the failed count and the total. Write a failing test first in the deploy-watch/db tests: a burst of limit-hit turns after a deploy must not raise a finding, and a real error burst still must. Then `citadel-test` on those files, citadel:self-review, and land with hand_off_land.
right: turnOutcomes leaves turns that stopped on a usage or rate limit out of the failed and total counts, so the deploy watch no longer blames a deploy for them.
